text:
Ben (Customer) Hey team — starting ~09:10 UTC we saw a big hit to our app. P95 jumped from ~700ms to ~4s and p99s are >12s. A bunch of requests are getting 429/504. Happened right after we moved a subset of traffic to model-rhino-3-small. Any idea?

Maya S. Thanks for flagging — can you paste a couple of example request ids / header traces? Are these long context requests or short chat turns?

Ben (Customer) Mostly short messages, ~200-400 tokens. Example header: 
```
X-Request-ID: req-8f3a2b
User: acct-274
model: rhino-3-small
seq_len: 512
```
A lot of the errors look like 504 gateway timeout then retry -> 429.

Raj P. (SRE) I'm seeing an alert: admission-queue-depth spiked on region-eu-west-1 cluster-17 at 09:09. worker_util averaged 98% and backlog grew to ~1200 concurrent queued requests. That matches p99 tail latency.

Dan R. (eng-runtime) rhino-3-small has higher per-request memory and slower decode on that kernel patch we rolled last week. Continuous batching combined with some long-running KV cache misses can cause head-of-line blocking. Could be batch scheduler holding short requests waiting for a large-seq request.

Carla O. (oncall) Can we confirm whether the canary rollout includes a runtime kernel change? infra-bot, show recent deploys to cluster-17.

infra-bot Deployed: 2026-03-15T08:55:02Z -> rhino-3-small kernel v1.9.3 (canary on cluster-17, weight 12%).

Maya S. Thanks. Ben — were you routed to cluster-17 for these requests?

Ben (Customer) Yes, majority were eu-west-1. I see request ids: req-8f3a2b, req-8f3a8c, req-8f4120. I can share HARs if helpful.

Raj P. (SRE) Repro plan: 1) capture a few request IDs, 2) check worker logs for req-* and kernel timeouts, 3) check batch sizes and whether a single oversized request held batches. I'll tail /var/log/runtime/serve.log on the nodes handling those IDs.

Dan R. (eng-runtime) Also check KV cache hit rates for those requests. If the canary introduced a regression in KV handling, cache misses will push more work to full decoding.

Carla O. (oncall) Immediate mitigations: 1) scale out cluster-17 by adding two extra worker pods (hot scale), 2) reduce canary weight back to baseline (roll back kernel v1.9.3), 3) enable per-route concurrency limits to avoid one customer grinding the pool. I'm going to run the scale now.

Maya S. Thanks. Ben, if we scale and rollback canary now, will you be able to verify from your side quickly?

Ben (Customer) Yes I can run a quick smoke after you toggle.

Carla O. (oncall) action: kubectl scale deployment/worker-cluster-17 --replicas=18 (+2)  (applied)

infra-bot Autoscaler: scale request acknowledged, provisioning nodes (expected 3m).

Dan R. (eng-runtime) Rolling canary rollback: setting rhino-3-small kernel v1.9.2 -> canary weight 0%. Doing gradual circuit drain on canary pods.

infra-bot Deployment change: rhino-3-small kernel weight set to 0% on cluster-17 (applied).

Raj P. (SRE) Observability: admission queue length trending down from 1200 -> 210 over 6m after scale and rollback. Worker_util down to ~65%. p95s on that route from 4.2s -> 820ms. p99s still a bit high at 2.1s but improving.

Ben (Customer) I see latency drop on our side — p95 back to ~900ms. A few 429s still creeping in but much better. Thanks.

Maya S. Followups we should do: 1) gather flame graphs for the canary kernel, 2) capture batch composition (how often large seqs block small ones), 3) add a rule to the router to isolate customers with >X long-seq concurrent requests into an isolation pool.

Dan R. (eng-runtime) Agreed. I want to instrument batch scheduler to emit a histogram of waiting times per request size and a breakdown of batch element seq_len distribution. I'll open a quick PR to add metrics: batch_wait_ms{seq_bucket=">256|256-1024|>1024"}.

Raj P. (SRE) Operational mitigation: set soft admission per node to 80 concurrent in cluster-17 for the route. This prevents queue growth if backend can't keep up. I'll update routing policy now.

infra-bot Routing update: route /generate model rhino-3-small max_concurrency=80 soft_admit=true (applied).

Ben (Customer) One last thing — we saw a cascade of client retries that made things worse. Any recommended retry settings?

Maya S. For now set client retry policy to exponential backoff with jitter, max_attempts=3, and treat 429 as a retryable but backoff-triggering code (increase base delay). We'll share recommended SDK settings in a follow-up note.

Dan R. (eng-runtime) Root cause hypothesis: kernel v1.9.3 introduced a regression where certain attention-pack kernels degrade with many small seq requests when continuous batching holds for larger seqs. That created head-of-line blocking and queue pileup.

Carla O. (oncall) Action items assigned: 
- Dan: produce metric PR + flamegraph for v1.9.3 regression (due EOD).
- Raj: keep soft_admit and monitor for 24h, add alert if admission_qdepth > 300 (done).
- Maya: send the customer SDK retry guidance and collect HARs for 5 failing req IDs.
- Infra: run postmortem if we see recurrence.

Ben (Customer) Appreciate the quick response. Will send HARs and verify after the scale.

Maya S. Thanks everyone — logging this as support ticket #98721. I'll follow up once we have flamegraphs and PR. :thumbsup:

Carla O. (oncall) Noting timeline: 09:09 alert -> 09:12 scale + rollback -> 09:18 improvements visible -> 09:50 steady. Leaving channel open for any regressions.
